notes: The two per-day caps above are published on the Observatory/Multiple page and are INDEPENDENT rules, not one rule. max_skies_per_day (8) is the stated ceiling and is also emergent -- 'it is possible to view up to eight different night skies in one day' follows from up to four Observatories per day (Chamber of Mirrors) times two viewing sources each (the room's own telescope, plus a held Telescope, which 'generates an additional night sky for each Observatory it is used in'). max_constellation_skies_per_day (7) is NOT derivable from those sources and is the load-bearing one: 'Regardless of how many night skies are available, only the first seven night skies generated per day can actually consist of constellations. For unknown reasons, if an eighth night sky is viewed, it is always empty.' The eighth sky is therefore VIEWABLE and comes back empty -- viewing it is not an illegal action, and modelling it as one would be a different mechanic.

BEWARE TWO UNRELATED SEVENS. max_constellation_skies_per_day (7) counts SKIES PER DAY. The largest single sky in the 'appearances' table below also happens to hold exactly 7 CONSTELLATIONS (at star counts 40 and 49, and nowhere else). The two sevens have no connection: one caps how many times you may look, the other is the widest partition the star values admit. env/obs.py's bound comment cites the sky-size seven; engine/constellations.py cites this per-day seven.

The same SpoilerBox independently confirms the live-star-count rule the generator depends on: 'All night skies determine their constellations based on the star count at the time that particular night sky is first viewed.' That is state.stars at view time, NOT the start-of-day GameConfig.stars snapshot -- the opposite convention from the Telescope's own spawn gate (engine/effects/items/telescope.py::gate), which deliberately reads cfg.stars so that a star earned mid-day cannot un-gate the item until tomorrow.

'grant' is present on exactly the records whose effect is an immediate resource delta, and is the sole source for the amount -- engine/game.py passes it to effects/tier1.py::_grant, the same grant path every room effect uses. 'resource' is one of that module's RESOURCES. 'effect' is the other half of the same idea and carries every non-resource effect that IS modelled, keyed by 'kind' and dispatched by engine/constellations.py::apply_effect: 'draft_bias' (names a data/priority_draws.json category_biases condition tag, whose own entry carries the magnitude), 'entrance_hall_trunks' (a container spawn), 'food_step_bonus' (raises one data/items.json dish's base step value). A record carries exactly one of 'grant' and 'effect' when implemented, and neither when not; tools/validate_data.py enforces that biconditional and checks each kind's payload against the file that owns it.

A night sky is fully determined by the star count at which it was first viewed that day: the constellations shown are the unique set whose star values SUM to that count (not a 'stars >= N' threshold), and no constellation appears twice in one sky. The 'appearances' table below is that partition for every count 0-49, inverted from the wiki's per-constellation appearance lists; tools/validate_data.py re-checks the sum for every count 1-49. Star count 0 is the sole exception and is asserted positively there: it shows the North Star (1 star) alone, and is reachable only by drafting an Observatory and then losing every star.

Only the eleven records with stars <= 20 take part in the 0-49 table. The Ink Well (50) and the Spiral of Stars (100) sit outside it: from 50 stars the Ink Well appears at EVERY count while the 0-49 partition repeats 50 lower, and from 100 the Spiral of Stars does the same against a 100-lower repeat (the Ink Well drops out over 100-149 and returns at 150). Above 200 the star values no longer sum to the count at all, so no table can express it; that range is out of scope.

'stacks' records whether re-activating the same constellation in one day repeats its effect, and it is READ, not decorative: engine/constellations.py::apply_effect refuses a non-stacking record's second activation outright, and food_step_bonus caps a non-stacking record's multiplier at one. The immediate resource grants stack (the wiki states The Twins keeps spawning trunks and Farmer's Apple keeps adding +3 steps per activation); the four day-long drafting/pricing effects -- Southern Cross, Draxus, The Sail, Florealis -- are each documented as having no additional effect on a second activation. The Ink Well's drafting option and the Spiral of Stars' word growth are likewise not per-activation (the Spiral gains its word when a sky containing it is GENERATED, not when it is activated).

Record order is ascending by 'stars' and is load-bearing: it is the single source for both the ACTIVATE_CONSTELLATION_BASE action block and the 'constellations' observation key in env/actions.py / env/obs.py, the same way data/locks.json's special_key_menu.order drives LOCK_SPECIAL_KEY_BASE. The nine implemented records' action ids unmask when their constellation is in an un-activated sky at the player's cell; the other four stay implemented: false and their ids are always masked.

The two day-scoped drafting flags GameState.southern_cross_active and GameState.draxus_active are read through engine/draft.py::_active_conditions against data/priority_draws.json's 'southern_cross_constellation' and 'draxus_constellation' category_biases entries, which carry the 40% and 30% magnitudes. Those two entries are category_biases, NOT priority_draws: a category bias re-deals an already-rolled slot, while a priority draw is an attempt-1 filter (docs/drafting.md). Activating the constellation is what sets each flag, and the 'effect' block below names the condition tag so the two files cannot drift apart unnoticed.

constellations.name: The Twins
constellations.effect_text: A pair of chests has been added to the entrance hall.

meta.notes: 'A pair of chests' is two, and because this record stacks, every activation adds another pair. They land in the same per-day counter the entrance_hall_trunk experiment effect bumps (SpecialItemsState.entrance_hall_trunks) and share its cap: the wiki calls this constellation's effect 'identical to triggering this effect twice'. The cap is deliberately NOT restated here -- it is read from experiments.json's entrance_hall_trunk record, the one place that publishes it, through the single check in SpecialItemsState.add_entrance_hall_trunks. 'There is no difference between a small chest and a regular trunk' (wiki), so these reuse the existing 'trunk' container kind.

constellations.name: Southern Cross
constellations.effect_text: Rooms with four doors are more common today.

meta.notes: The magnitude is not here on purpose: activating this only sets the day-scoped GameState.southern_cross_active, and the 40% four-way re-deal is priority_draws.json's 'southern_cross_constellation' category_biases entry, which owns the chance, the Mechanarium/Chamber-of-Mirrors exclusions and the upgrade-variant filter. 'condition' names that entry so validate_data.py can check the two files still agree.

+3 steps per apple per activation, and it stacks. The worked example the wiki publishes -- seven activations plus a Salt Shaker and a Silver Spoon taking one apple to 48 steps -- is what fixes the pipeline ORDER as well as the number: (2 + 7*3 + 1) * 2 = 48 only if the bonus raises the apple's own base (items.json food.dishes.apple.steps = 2) BEFORE special_items.py::food_steps folds in the Salt Shaker's flat +1 and the Silver Spoon's doubling. Applying it after the fold would give 2*2 + 21 = 25, or (2+1)*2 + 21 = 27. 'food_id' keys the dish rather than hardcoding apples in Python, so the bonus reaches all three apple varieties (they share the one dish id) and nothing else.

constellations.name: Draxus, the Dead
constellations.effect_text: Dead-end rooms are more common today.

meta.notes: Same shape as southern_cross: activation sets GameState.draxus_active and the 30% dead-end re-deal lives in priority_draws.json's 'draxus_constellation' category_biases entry. Not to be confused with cloister_of_draxus__ix36's own, unrelated 'only Dead Ends draftable from this room' rule -- the shared name is theming, not a shared mechanism.
